questions.article: Realizing the True Purpose in Life
questions.q: Why does the article say that earning, building a house and raising one’s standard of living do not amount to a purposeful life?
options: They are driven by needs and desires, the same urge for survival that moves an animal
Yes. Man’s true purpose must reflect his nobler side.
They benefit only other people
Not quite. The article says: They are driven by needs and desires, the same urge for survival that moves an animal.
They are forbidden activities
Not quite. The article says: They are driven by needs and desires, the same urge for survival that moves an animal.
They take too much time
Not quite. The article says: They are driven by needs and desires, the same urge for survival that moves an animal.
questions.rationale: “The motive force behind these actions is the same urge that motivates an animal in various ways, i.e. its concern for its own survival.”

questions.article: Realizing the True Purpose in Life
questions.q: How does the article describe the month of fasting?
options: A month for feasting at night
Not quite. The article says: A month of abstinence and control that lifts us above material pursuits – not of indulgence after a few hours of hunger.
A month of abstinence and control that lifts us above material pursuits – not of indulgence after a few hours of hunger
Right. Training for the other eleven months.
A month chiefly for social gatherings
Not quite. The article says: A month of abstinence and control that lifts us above material pursuits – not of indulgence after a few hours of hunger.
A month of rest from responsibility
Not quite. The article says: A month of abstinence and control that lifts us above material pursuits – not of indulgence after a few hours of hunger.
questions.rationale: “It is a month of abstinence and control, not a month of indulgence after a few hours of ritualistic hunger and thirst.”

questions.q: According to the article, why has God placed signs in the visible world?
options: To decorate the earth
Not quite. The article says: To make it easier to believe in hidden realities, by reflecting them in things we can see.
To replace the need for reflection
Not quite. The article says: To make it easier to believe in hidden realities, by reflecting them in things we can see.
To make it easier to believe in hidden realities, by reflecting them in things we can see
Yes. The sky suggests His might; wind and water, His mercy.
To test who can count them
Not quite. The article says: To make it easier to believe in hidden realities, by reflecting them in things we can see.
questions.rationale: “God requires man to believe in certain hidden realities. To make this easier, He has set up material symbols of these realities in the outside world.”

questions.q: A visitor once told Maulana there was “no news.” How did Maulana reply?
options: That no news is good news
Not quite. The article says: Every day a new sun rises and the universe moves in perfect order – is that not news?.
That newspapers should be read more carefully
Not quite. The article says: Every day a new sun rises and the universe moves in perfect order – is that not news?.
Every day a new sun rises and the universe moves in perfect order – is that not news?
Well read. Real news is what nourishes God-realization.
That news is of no importance
Not quite. The article says: Every day a new sun rises and the universe moves in perfect order – is that not news?.
questions.rationale: “Every day a new sun rises, the whole universe is moving in high order—isn’t that news?”

questions.q: What does the article see in the rite of sa’i, the running between Safa and Marwah?
options: A race among the pilgrims
Not quite. The article says: Every pilgrim is commanded to follow in the footsteps of a woman, Hajar.
A custom with no known origin
Not quite. The article says: Every pilgrim is commanded to follow in the footsteps of a woman, Hajar.
Every pilgrim is commanded to follow in the footsteps of a woman, Hajar
Correct. A demonstration of woman’s honoured position.
A rite performed by women only
Not quite. The article says: Every pilgrim is commanded to follow in the footsteps of a woman, Hajar.
questions.rationale: “Perhaps there could be no better demonstration of a woman’s greatness than God’s command to men, literally to follow in her footsteps.”

questions.article: Acknowledging the Role of Prof Farida Khanam
questions.q: What had made an English translation of Maulana’s book seem impossible, and how was it overcome?
options: The original English sources of its quotations had been lost; Farida Khanam traced them in libraries and translated the book
Yes. It appeared as God Arises.
It was too long; she shortened it
Not quite. The article says: The original English sources of its quotations had been lost; Farida Khanam traced them in libraries and translated the book.
No publisher would accept it; she printed it herself
Not quite. The article says: The original English sources of its quotations had been lost; Farida Khanam traced them in libraries and translated the book.
The Urdu was too difficult; she simplified it
Not quite. The article says: The original English sources of its quotations had been lost; Farida Khanam traced them in libraries and translated the book.
questions.rationale: “She tirelessly began searching for the original English texts in various libraries… Eventually, she managed to acquire all the English excerpts and proceeded to translate the entire book.”

questions.article: Acknowledging the Role of Prof Farida Khanam
questions.q: At a conference in Switzerland Maulana was asked overnight for a document on peace and felt unable to produce it. What was his daughter’s response?
options: “Ask for more time”
Not quite. The article says: “We have the entire night. We will pray to God and stay awake to prepare it”.
“Let the professors do it”
Not quite. The article says: “We have the entire night. We will pray to God and stay awake to prepare it”.
“It cannot be done”
Not quite. The article says: “We have the entire night. We will pray to God and stay awake to prepare it”.
“We have the entire night. We will pray to God and stay awake to prepare it”
Right. It was ready by dawn and warmly accepted.
questions.rationale: “‘We have the entire night,’ she declared. ‘We will pray to God and stay awake to prepare it.’”

questions.q: “Your freedom ends where my nose begins.” Which principle does the article illustrate with this story?
options: Rules apply only to strangers
Not quite. The article says: Non-interference – each acting within his own sphere, as the stars keep to their orbits.
The strong may do as they wish
Not quite. The article says: Non-interference – each acting within his own sphere, as the stars keep to their orbits.
Freedom has no limits
Not quite. The article says: Non-interference – each acting within his own sphere, as the stars keep to their orbits.
Non-interference – each acting within his own sphere, as the stars keep to their orbits
Yes. Order prevails when no one trespasses on another.
questions.rationale: “Order prevails when everyone functions within their own sphere, taking care never to trespass upon the domains of their fellow human beings.”

questions.q: A returning spacecraft is red hot outside yet comfortable within. What lesson for life does the article draw?
options: Do not let outward heat – others’ anger or hostility – enter within; stay calm and forgiving inside
Exactly. That is how one comes safely through a crisis.
Travel as little as possible
Not quite. The article says: Do not let outward heat – others’ anger or hostility – enter within; stay calm and forgiving inside.
Answer heat with heat
Not quite. The article says: Do not let outward heat – others’ anger or hostility – enter within; stay calm and forgiving inside.
Avoid all difficult situations
Not quite. The article says: Do not let outward heat – others’ anger or hostility – enter within; stay calm and forgiving inside.
questions.rationale: “There is only one way to survive under such conditions, and that is by not letting oneself be inwardly affected by one’s outward situation.”

questions.q: How, according to the answer given, can a believer who fasts contribute positively to society?
options: By keeping apart from society
Not quite. The article says: By realising that God is the Giver and he the taker, and so becoming a “giver” member of society.
By realising that God is the Giver and he the taker, and so becoming a “giver” member of society
Well read. Giving to others what one receives.
By fasting more days than required
Not quite. The article says: By realising that God is the Giver and he the taker, and so becoming a “giver” member of society.
By persuading others to fast
Not quite. The article says: By realising that God is the Giver and he the taker, and so becoming a “giver” member of society.
questions.rationale: “The profound feeling of God being the Giver and one’s own self being the ‘taker’ should inspire him to become a ‘giver’ member of the society.”
